Read in and preprocess raw data

Code
# species_pattern - either "", "^mm10---" or "^GRCh38-"

read_raw <- function(i,
                     samples_tsv,
                     species_pattern = "",
                     organism = NULL,
                     ncount_min = NA,
                     ncount_max = NA,
                     mt_percent_max = NA,
                     save_qs_dir = "output/seurat_objects/individual/",
                     h5_folder = "/home/gdrobertslab/lab/Counts_2/",
                     min_n_cells = 50,
                     annotate_ref,
                     annotate_labels,
                     annotate_species = "",
                     annotate_additional_ref,
                     annotate_additional_labels,
                     bam_file) {
    sample_name <- samples_tsv$Sample_ID[i]

    # Not making this an lapply as defaults are different, may do it later
    ncount_min <-
        pick_cutoff(
            ncount_min,
            samples_tsv$subset_nCount_RNA_min[i],
            0,
            species_pattern
        )
    ncount_max <-
        pick_cutoff(
            ncount_max,
            samples_tsv$subset_nCount_RNA_max[i],
            Inf,
            species_pattern
        )
    mt_percent_max <-
        pick_cutoff(
            mt_percent_max,
            samples_tsv$subset_percent.mt_max[i],
            100,
            species_pattern
        )

    path_h5 <-
        paste0(h5_folder, "/", sample_name, "/filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5")

    counts <- tibble::tibble(sample_name = sample_name)

    if (!file.exists(path_h5)) {
        stop(paste(sample_name, "h5 file does not exist"))
    } else {
        sobj <-
            rrrSingleCellUtils::tenx_load_qc(
                h5_file = path_h5,
                species_pattern = species_pattern,
                violin_plot = FALSE
            )

        sobj$bam_file <- bam_file

        sobj$cell_barcode <- Seurat::Cells(sobj)

        pre_filt_hist <-
            rrrSingleCellUtils::feature_hist(
                sobj,
                features = c("nCount_RNA", "percent.mt"),
                cutoff_table = tibble::tibble(
                    feature = c("nCount_RNA", "percent.mt"),
                    min_val = c(ncount_min, mt_percent_max),
                    max_val = c(ncount_max, NA)
                )
            )

        counts$n_cells_pre_filter <- ncol(sobj)

        counts$n_cells_post_filter <-
            sobj@meta.data %>%
            as.data.frame() %>%
            filter(
                nCount_RNA > ncount_min &
                    nCount_RNA < ncount_max &
                    percent.mt < mt_percent_max
            ) %>%
            nrow()

        if (counts$n_cells_post_filter >= min_n_cells) {
            counts$kept <- TRUE
            sobj <-
                subset(
                    sobj,
                    nCount_RNA > ncount_min &
                        nCount_RNA < ncount_max &
                        percent.mt < mt_percent_max
                ) %>%
                rrrSingleCellUtils::process_seurat()

            opt_res <-
                rrrSingleCellUtils::optimize_silhouette(
                    sobj,
                    summary_plot = FALSE
                ) %>%
                dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(sil_vals)) %>%
                dplyr::pull(res_vals) %>%
                head(1)

            sobj <- Seurat::FindClusters(sobj, resolution = opt_res)

            sobj$individ_clusters <- sobj$seurat_clusters

            # Add metadata to Seurat object from samples_tsv
            for (colname in colnames(samples_tsv)) {
                sobj[[colname]] <- samples_tsv[[colname]][i]
            }

            # Annotate celltypes
            sobj <-
                rrrSingleCellUtils::annotate_celltypes(
                    sobj,
                    species = annotate_species,
                    ref = annotate_ref,
                    labels = annotate_labels,
                    add_ref = annotate_additional_ref,
                    add_labels = annotate_additional_labels,
                    aggr_ref = TRUE
                )

            dimplot_fig <-
                Seurat::DimPlot(
                    sobj,
                    group.by = c("individ_clusters", "cell_type"),
                    label = TRUE,
                    label.size = 2,
                    label.box = TRUE,
                    repel = TRUE,
                    ncol = 1
                ) +
                Seurat::NoLegend()

            ggplot2::ggsave(
                paste0(
                    "output/figures/qc_cutoffs/pre_filter_hist_",
                    sample_name,
                    dplyr::if_else(
                        organism == "",
                        "",
                        paste0("_", organism)
                    ),
                    ".pdf"
                ),
                patchwork::wrap_plots(
                    pre_filt_hist,
                    dimplot_fig,
                    ncol = 1,
                    heights = c(1, 5)
                ),
                width = 10,
                height = 20
            )

            qs::qsave(
                sobj,
                dplyr::if_else(
                    organism == "",
                    paste0(save_qs_dir, "/", sample_name, ".qs"),
                    paste0(save_qs_dir, "/", sample_name, "_", organism, ".qs")
                )
            )

            message(sample_name, " sobject made and saved")
        } else {
            counts$kept <- FALSE
            message(
                paste0(
                    sample_name,
                    " started with ",
                    ncol(sobj),
                    " cells but has ",
                    counts$n_cells_post_filter,
                    " cells left after filtering which is less than ",
                    min_n_cells,
                    " hence it was discarded"
                )
            )
        }
    }

    counts$median_ncount <-
        median(sobj$nCount_RNA)

    counts$mean_ncount <-
        mean(sobj$nCount_RNA)

    return(counts)
}

pick_cutoff <- function(arg_provided,
                        from_sample_tsv,
                        default,
                        species_pattern) {
    from_sample_tsv <- pull_species_cutoff(from_sample_tsv, species_pattern)
    if (is.na(arg_provided)) {
        if (is.na(from_sample_tsv)) {
            return(default)
        } else {
            return(from_sample_tsv)
        }
    } else {
        return(arg_provided)
    }
}

# Pull the cutoff value from the sample tsv data if it's in there
pull_species_cutoff <- function(from_sample_tsv,
                                species_pattern) {
    if (species_pattern != "") {
        if (!grepl(
            # we don't want the caret in the pattern for this
            stringr::str_remove(species_pattern, "^\\^"),
            from_sample_tsv
        )) {
            stop(
                "Species pattern provided but not found in from_sample_tsv. ",
                "Species_pattern: ",
                species_pattern,
                ". Cutoff info from sample sheet: ",
                from_sample_tsv
            )
        }
        cutoff <-
            stringr::str_match(
                from_sample_tsv,
                paste0(stringr::str_remove(species_pattern, "\\^"), "([0-9]+)")
            )[1, 2]
        return(as.numeric(cutoff))
    } else {
        # If from_sample_tsv has letters in it, species pattern likely there
        # We need to specify scientific = F so that 100,000 != 1e+05 which
        # has an "e" :-| and so fails here
        if (grepl("[a-zA-Z]", format(from_sample_tsv, scientific = FALSE)) &&
            !is.na(from_sample_tsv)) {
            stop(
                "Sample cutoff value is not just a number but species_pattern ",
                "not provided. Species_pattern: ",
                species_pattern,
                ". Cutoff from sample sheet: ",
                from_sample_tsv
            )
            # Otherwise it's either a number or NA
        } else {
            return(from_sample_tsv)
        }
    }
}

read_raw_from_table <- function(sample_table,
                                h5_folder,
                                min_n_cells = 1000,
                                organism,
                                annotate_species,
                                count_table_file,
                                bam_file,
                                annotate_additional_ref = list(),
                                annotate_additional_labels = list()) {
    count_table <- parallel::mclapply(
        seq_len(nrow(sample_table)),
        mc.preschedule = FALSE,
        mc.cores = parallelly::availableCores(),
        function(i) {
            read_raw(
                i = i,
                h5_folder = h5_folder,
                min_n_cells = min_n_cells,
                sample_table,
                organism = organism,
                annotate_species = annotate_species,
                bam_file =
                    paste0(
                        h5_folder,
                        "/",
                        sample_table$Sample_ID[i],
                        "/",
                        bam_file
                    ),
                annotate_additional_ref = annotate_additional_ref,
                annotate_additional_labels = annotate_additional_labels
            )
        }
    ) |>
        confirm_mclapply_worked() |>
        dplyr::bind_rows()

    readr::write_tsv(count_table, count_table_file)
}

gsea_dotplot <- function(data, x_col = "z_score") {
    lab4plot <-
        tibble::tibble(
            y = c(-2.5, 2.5),
            x = c(0.2, 0.2),
            label = c("Downregulated", "Upregulated")
        )

    plot_name <-
        ggplot2::ggplot() +
        ggplot2::geom_point(
            data = data,
            ggplot2::aes(
                x = -1 * order,
                y = get(x_col),
                color = -log10(padj),
                size = size
            ),
            stat = "identity",
            alpha = 0.8
        ) +
        ggplot2::coord_flip() +
        ggplot2::geom_text(
            data = data, # text for pathways names
            aes(
                x = -1 * order,
                y = get(x_col) + (y_pos * 5),
                hjust = justify_y,
                label = pathway
            ),
            size = 2,
            fontface = "bold"
        ) +
        geom_text(
            data = lab4plot, # text for upregulated/downregulated
            aes(
                x = x,
                y = y,
                label = label
            ),
            fontface = "bold",
            size = 2.5
        ) +
        ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
            values = rrrSingleCellUtils::plot_cols,
            name = paste0(x_col, " > 0")
        ) +
        ggplot2::theme(
            strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(
                color = "white",
                fill = "white"
            ),
            panel.grid.major = ggplot2::element_blank(),
            panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
            panel.border = ggplot2::element_blank(),
            axis.line.x = ggplot2::element_line(color = "black"),
            axis.line.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
            axis.title.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7),
            axis.ticks.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
            plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7, face = "bold"),
            axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
            axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7),
            legend.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7, face = "bold")
        ) +
        ggplot2::labs(
            title = data$sample[1],
            y = "NES",
            x = ""
        ) +
        ggplot2::theme(plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
        ggplot2::ylim(-6, 6) +
        ggplot2::scale_color_gradient(low = plot_cols[2], high = plot_cols[1])

    return(plot_name)
}

#' Check for HDF5 File Support
#'
#' This function checks for the availability of HDF5 file support in the current R environment.
#'
#' @return Logical value indicating whether HDF5 support is available.
hdf5_check <- function() {
    h5_return <-
        suppressWarnings(
            try(
                system(
                    "which h5pfc",
                    intern = TRUE,
                    ignore.stderr = TRUE
                )
            )
        ) |>
            length() > 0
    if (!h5_return) {
        stop(
            "\nYou need to have h5pfc installed to read in h5_files. ",
            "Perhaps ml load HDF5 before you start R?\n"
        )
    }
}

Confirm that Seurat version installed is > 5

Code
#' Check Seurat Version
#'
#' This function checks the version of the Seurat package installed in the R environment.
#' It ensures that the correct version of Seurat is being used for downstream analysis.
#'
#' @return A message indicating the version of Seurat installed.
seurat_version_check <- function() {
    if (packageVersion("Seurat") < "5.0.0") {
        stop(
            "Please install Seurat version 5.0.0 or higher. ",
            "You are currently using version ",
            packageVersion("Seurat")
        )
    }
}
Code
#' Confirm mclapply Worked And Dump Error Messages If Not
#'
#' This function checks if the `mclapply` function executed successfully on the provided input list.
#'
#' @param input_list A list that was processed by `mclapply`.
#' @return The input list if `mclapply` was successful or the error messages if it failed.
confirm_mclapply_worked <- function(input_list) {
    if (length(input_list) == 0) {
        stop("Empty input list")
    }

    has_error <- FALSE
    for (item in input_list) {
        if (inherits(item, "try-error")) {
            warning("mclapply failed with error: ", item[[1]])
            has_error <- TRUE
        }
    }

    if (has_error) {
        stop("mclapply failed")
    } else {
        return(input_list)
    }
}

Samples for downsample analysis

Code
filter_cells_umi_cutoff <- function(sobj, max_umi) {
    keep_cells <-
        sobj |>
        SeuratObject::FetchData(vars = c(
            "cell_group",
            "cell_barcode",
            "bam_file",
            "nCount_RNA"
        )) |>
        tibble::as_tibble() |>
        dplyr::group_by(cell_group) |>
        dplyr::arrange(cell_group, cell_barcode) |>
        dplyr::mutate(cumsum = cumsum(nCount_RNA)) |>
        dplyr::filter(cumsum < max_umi) |>
        dplyr::pull(cell_barcode)

    sobj_sub <- subset(sobj, cells = keep_cells)
    return(sobj_sub)
}

filter_cells_n_cell_cutoff <- function(sobj, n_cells) {
    set.seed(1337)
    sobj <- subset(sobj, downsample = n_cells)

    return(sobj)
}

make_cbt <- function(sobj, cutoff, downsample_type) {
    if (downsample_type == "max_umi") {
        sub_sobj <- filter_cells_umi_cutoff(sobj, cutoff)
    } else if (downsample_type == "n_cells") {
        sub_sobj <- filter_cells_n_cell_cutoff(sobj, cutoff)
    } else {
        stop("Must provide either max_umi or n_cells as downsample type")
    }

    cell_barcode_group_table <-
        sub_sobj |>
        SeuratObject::FetchData(vars = c(
            "cell_group",
            "cell_barcode",
            "bam_file",
            "nCount_RNA"
        )) |>
        tibble::as_tibble() |>
        dplyr::arrange(cell_group)

    return(cell_barcode_group_table)
}

scanbit_downsample_loop <- function(sobj,
                                    cutoff_vector,
                                    out_dir_base,
                                    sample_label,
                                    min_read_depth = 5,
                                    min_snvs_per_cluster = 10,
                                    downsample_type = "n_cells",
                                    keep_temp_dir = FALSE,
                                    ploidy,
                                    ref_fasta) {
    parallel::mclapply(
        cutoff_vector,
        mc.cores = 10,
        mc.preschedule = FALSE,
        function(cutoff) {
            out_dir <-
                file.path(
                    out_dir_base,
                    paste0(
                        "downsample_",
                        sprintf("%.0f", cutoff),
                        "_cells"
                    )
                )

            dir.create(
                out_dir,
                recursive = TRUE,
                showWarnings = FALSE
            )

            if (keep_temp_dir) {
                temp_dir <- file.path(out_dir_base, "tempdir")
                cleanup <- FALSE
            } else {
                temp_dir <- tempfile(
                    pattern = paste0(
                        "tempdir_",
                        cutoff,
                        sample_label
                    )
                )
                cleanup <- TRUE
            }

            # Get the cell barcodes for the current cutoff
            cell_barcode_group_table <-
                make_cbt(
                    sobj,
                    cutoff = cutoff,
                    downsample_type = downsample_type
                )

            readr::write_tsv(
                cell_barcode_group_table,
                file.path(
                    out_dir,
                    paste0(
                        "cell_barcode_table_",
                        sample_label,
                        "_",
                        sprintf("%.0f", cutoff),
                        "_cells.txt"
                    )
                )
            )

            cell_barcode_group_table <-
                dplyr::select(cell_barcode_group_table, -nCount_RNA)

            scanBit::get_snp_tree(
                cellid_bam_table = cell_barcode_group_table,
                ploidy = ploidy,
                temp_dir = temp_dir,
                output_dir = out_dir,
                output_base_name = paste0(
                    "downsample_",
                    sample_label,
                    "_",
                    sprintf("%.0f", cutoff)
                ),
                ref_fasta = ref_fasta,
                min_depth = min_read_depth,
                job_base = "downsample_cells",
                min_snvs_per_cluster = min_snvs_per_cluster,
                n_bootstraps = 10000,
                max_prop_missing_at_site = 0.9,
                cleanup = cleanup,
                tree_image_type = "pdf",
                other_job_header_options = c(
                    "--time=8:00:00",
                    "--partition=himem,general"
                ),
                other_batch_options = c(
                    "ml purge",
                    "ml miniforge3",
                    'eval "$(conda shell.bash hook)"'
                ),
            )
        }
    )
}

Helper function to run scanbit

This asssumes a bunch of things about the structure of this project ::: {.cell}

scanbit_one_sample <- function(this_sample,
                               species,
                               ploidy,
                               ref_fasta,
                               out_dir) {
    sobj <-
        qs::qread(paste0(
            "output/seurat_objects/individual/",
            this_sample,
            "_",
            species,
            ".qs"
        ))

    sobj$cell_group <-
        paste0(
            sobj$cluster_label,
            "_c",
            sobj$individ_clusters
        )

    cell_barcode_group_table <-
        sobj@meta.data |>
        dplyr::select(cell_group, cell_barcode, bam_file) |>
        dplyr::as_tibble()

    job_worked <-
        scanBit::get_snp_tree(
            cellid_bam_table = cell_barcode_group_table,
            ploidy = ploidy,
            output_dir = out_dir,
            temp_dir = paste0("/gpfs0/scratch/mvc002/scanbit/", this_sample),
            output_base_name = paste0("snvs_", this_sample),
            ref_fasta = ref_fasta,
            min_depth = c(5, 10, 20, 30),
            job_base = paste0("sb_", this_sample),
            log_base = paste0("slurmOut/snv_", this_sample),
            min_snvs_per_cluster = 200,
            n_bootstraps = 10000,
            max_prop_missing_at_site = 0.9,
            tree_image_type = "pdf",
            cleanup = TRUE,
            other_job_header_options = c(
                "--time=8:00:00",
                "--partition=himem,general"
            ),
            other_batch_options = c(
                "ml purge",
                "ml miniforge3",
                'eval "$(conda shell.bash hook)"'
            ),
        )

    return(job_worked)
}

#' ggsave_wrap
#'
#' A wrapper function for saving a single ggplot object in multiple file formats at once.
#'
#' This function simplifies the process of saving a ggplot object by allowing the user
#' to specify multiple file formats and save the plot in all of them with a single call.
#'
#' @param file_stub The base file name (without extension) to use for saving the plot.
#' @param file_types A character vector of file extensions (e.g., c(".png", ".pdf")).
#' @param plot_variable The ggplot object to be saved.
#' @param width The width of the saved plot.
#' @param height The height of the saved plot.
#'
#' @return The function does not return a value but saves the plot to the specified files.
#'
#' @examples
#' # Example usage:
#' # ggsave_wrap("my_plot", c(".png", ".pdf"), my_plot, width = 6, height = 4)
#'
#' @export
ggsave_wrap <- function(
    file_stub,
    file_types,
    plot_variable,
    width,
    height
) {
    files_made <-
        lapply(
            file_types,
            function(x) {
                ggplot2::ggsave(
                    paste0(file_stub, ".", x),
                    plot_variable,
                    width = width,
                    height = height
                )
            }
        )
}

Check required software is available

For these analysis we are going to do some key validations and analyses.

  • Run variant calling on 10x flex data to quantify the sequencing error rate at varying read depths.
    • Data from https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/40k-mixture-of-cells-dissociated-from-4-fixed-mouse-tissues-using-manual-dissociation-multiplexed-samples-4-probe-barcodes-1-standard
  • Analyze samples where the tumor cells express a marker that allows us to know which cells should be called as tumor and then assess accuracy of the method.
    • S0105 - K7M2-RFP tibia tumor
    • S0122 - K7M2 sLPmCherry lung mets 10 days post injection. Flow sorted Cherry positive fraction 1:1:1 mix of CD45+, Epcam+ and double negative
    • GSE247228 - lentiviral green fluorescent protein (GFP) in melanoma cells
    • GSE201615 - Cas9 in soft-tissue sarcoma cells, also dsRED
    • S0260 - barcoded F420 tumor samples
    • S0261 - barcoded F420 tumor sample
  • Analyze samples from genetically distinct mouse strains where we know how the clustering should look.
    • S0066 - B6 lung
    • S0074 - Balb/c lung
  • Analyze mouse OS models where the tumor cells derive from the host mouse strain to simulate a genetic divergence more expected in patients.
    • S0066 - (control) B6 lung
    • S0067 - B6, F420 injected, lungs from ROB 273 A, B, D; Epcam postive:negative 1:1
    • S0068 - B6, F420 injected, lungs from ROB 273E and ROB 274A; Epcam postive:negative 1:1
    • S0074 - (control) Balb/c lung
    • S0075 - Balb/c, K7M2 injected, lungs; Epcam postive:negative 1:1
    • S0105 - K7M2-RFP tibia tumor
    • S0200 - (control) F420 cellculture p17
    • S0201 - (control) K7M2 cellculture p17
    • S0246 - F420 lung mets and niche cells ctrl
    • S0259 - (control) F420, barcoded, preinjection t0 ctrl
    • S0260 - barcoded F420 tumor samples
    • S0261 - barcoded F420 tumor sample
  • Assess scanBit results when run on human patient tumor samples.
    • GSE152048 OS samples
    • GSE162454 OS samples
    • GSE210358 prostate cancer samples
    • GSE222703 renal cell carcinoma samples
    • GSE169396 bone samples
    • GSE237579 healthy PBMC samples

Read in raw data and process to Seurat objects

The metadata for all samples is stored in misc/sample_metadata.tsv.

Note that in the sample_metadata, for samples with multiple references, the cutoff format is “GRCh38-40000;mm10—20000” where the species_pattern is at the beginning of the string, followed by the cutoff value (no dash or anything). This is split from the second cutoff value by a semicolon. If there is only one reference, just use the cutoff value, no species pattern is needed.

Prep the flex data

We’re going to run scanBit on a merged object for this so the data all ends up in one BCF file. ::: {.cell}

Code
flex_samples <-
    read_tsv("misc/flex_metadata.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    pull(Sample_ID)

flex_sobj_list <-
    lapply(
        flex_samples,
        function(this_sample) {
            qs::qread(paste0(
                "output/seurat_objects/individual/",
                this_sample,
                "_mouse.qs"
            ))
        }
    )

merged_flex <-
    merge(flex_sobj_list[[1]], flex_sobj_list[-1]) %>%
    process_seurat()

merged_flex$cell_group <-
    paste0(
        merged_flex$cluster_label,
        "_c",
        merged_flex$individ_clusters
    )

flex_dimplot <-
    (DimPlot(
        merged_flex,
        group.by = "Name",
        label = TRUE,
        label.box = TRUE,
        label.size = 2,
        repel = TRUE,
        ncol = 1
    ) +
        NoLegend()) +
    (DimPlot(
        merged_flex,
        group.by = "cell_group",
        label = TRUE,
        label.box = TRUE,
        label.size = 2,
        repel = TRUE,
        ncol = 1
    ) +
        NoLegend()) +
    (DimPlot(
        merged_flex,
        group.by = "cell_type",
        label = TRUE,
        label.box = TRUE,
        label.size = 2,
        repel = TRUE,
        ncol = 1
    ) +
        NoLegend())

ggsave(
    "output/figures/dimplot_flex_cell_type_group.pdf",
    flex_dimplot,
    width = 10,
    height = 20
)

flex_cell_barcode_group_table <-
    merged_flex@meta.data %>%
    select(cell_group, cell_barcode, bam_file) %>%
    as_tibble()

Calculate variant calling accuracy in flex data

Any mutation called in the flex data is almost certainly a PCR/sequencing error since this method uses probes. ::: {.cell}

Code
all_flex_files <-
    list.files(
        path = "output/flex/var_counts_d1",
        pattern = ".txt",
        full.names = TRUE
    )

# In the future, break this down by mt vs non-mt to see if the non-mt are the wierd inaccurate calls ~ 500 - 1000 depth
flex_accuracy <-
    read_tsv(
        all_flex_files,
        id = "sample",
        show_col_types = FALSE,
        col_names = c("chr", "alt", "depth", "count")
    ) %>%
    mutate(
        sample = basename(sample) %>%
            str_remove(".txt"),
        alt = if_else(
            alt == ".",
            "ref",
            "variant"
        )
    ) %>%
    group_by(sample, depth, alt) %>%
    summarize(count = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(sample, depth) %>%
    mutate(total_count = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    pivot_wider(
        id_cols = c(sample, depth, total_count),
        names_from = "alt",
        values_from = "count",
        values_fill = 0
    ) %>%
    mutate(perc_wrong = variant / total_count * 100) %>%
    group_by(depth) %>%
    summarize(
        mean_total_count = mean(total_count, na.rm = TRUE),
        mean_perc_wrong = mean(perc_wrong, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(depth != 1)

write_tsv(
    flex_accuracy,
    "output/flex/flex_accuracy.txt"
)

accuracy_plot <-
    filter(flex_accuracy, depth <= 50) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = depth, y = mean_perc_wrong / 100)) +
    #geom_smooth(alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_point() +
    # geom_text(
    #     data = filter(flex_accuracy, depth <= 10),
    #     aes(label = depth),
    #     nudge_y = 0.00001
    # ) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
    labs(
        title = "Percent Inaccurate Calls by Read Depth",
        x = "Read depth of variant calls",
        y = "% inaccurate variant calls"
    )

ggsave_wrap(
    "output/figures/flex_accuracy_scatterplot",
    file_type = c("png", "pdf"),
    plot_variable = accuracy_plot,
    width = 6,
    height = 4
)

    mutate(total_count = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    pivot_wider(
        id_cols = c(sample, depth, total_count),
        names_from = "alt",
        values_from = "count",
        values_fill = 0
    ) %>%
    mutate(perc_wrong = variant / ref * 100) %>%
    group_by(depth) %>%
    summarize(
        mean_total_count = mean(total_count, na.rm = TRUE),
        mean_perc_wrong = mean(perc_wrong, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(depth != 1)

flex_accuracy %>%
    filter(depth <= 20) %>%
    gt::gt() %>%
    gt::cols_label(
        depth = gt::md("**Read depth**"),
        mean_total_count = gt::md("**Average covered bases**"),
        mean_perc_wrong = gt::md("**% inaccurate variant calls**")
    ) %>%
    gt::fmt_percent(
        columns = "mean_perc_wrong",
        scale_values = FALSE,
        decimals = 4
    ) %>%
    gt::fmt_number(columns = "mean_total_count") %>%
    gt::cols_align(
        align = "center"
    ) %>%
    gt::gtsave(
        filename = "output/figures/flex_accuracy_table.html"
    )

Plot how many sites are covered at each depth

Plot how many inaccurate variant calls we would expect at each depth

Downsample GEO samples to one cell and quantify read depth coverage

Run scanBit on individual cells with min_read_depth of 1 to use for read depth and accuracy analysis

For this I’m keeping ten individual cells per cluster, and each cell is assigned to its own cell_group so that I am calculating read depth data for many individual cells. ::: {.cell}

Code
samples_geo <-
    read_tsv("misc/validation_geo_metadata.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    filter(grepl("tumor validation|healthy samples", sample_group)) %>%
    pull(Sample_ID) %>%
    unique()

n_cell_cutoffs <- 1

# Keeping mc.cores low since each run submits 100+ jobs
output <-
    parallel::mclapply(
        samples_geo,
        mc.cores = 2,
        mc.preschedule = FALSE,
        function(this_sample) {
            sobj <-
                qs::qread(paste0(
                    "output/seurat_objects/individual/",
                    this_sample,
                    "_human.qs"
                ))

            sobj$cell_group <-
                paste0(
                    "clust_",
                    sobj$individ_clusters,
                    "_",
                    sobj$cell_barcode
                )

            Idents(sobj) <- sobj$individ_clusters
            set.seed(1337)
            sobj <- subset(sobj, downsample = 10)

            Idents(sobj) <-
                sobj$cell_group

            scanbit_downsample_loop(
                sobj,
                cutoff_vector = n_cell_cutoffs,
                min_read_depth = c(1, 2, 5, 10, 20),
                out_dir_base = file.path(
                    "output/read_depth/scanbit_out/geo_samples/",
                    this_sample
                ),
                keep_temp_dir = TRUE,
                sample_label = this_sample,
                ploidy = "GRCh38",
                ref_fasta = "/home/gdrobertslab/lab/GenRef/10x-hg38/fasta/genome.fa"
            )
        }
    )

        names_to = "depth",

    group_by(depth) %>%
    summarize(
        mean_count_var = mean(count),
        median_count_var = median(count),

Code
shared_files <-
    list.files(
        path = "output/read_depth/shared",
        pattern = "shared.+\\.txt",
        full.names = TRUE
    )

parse_shared <- function(file_name) {
    dataset <- read_tsv(
        file_name,
        name_repair = "minimal",
        show_col_types = FALSE,
        id = "dataset"
    ) |>
        mutate(
            dataset = str_remove(dataset, ".+shared_") |>
                str_remove(".txt")
        ) |>
        pivot_longer(
            cols = starts_with("clust"),
            names_to = "cell_2",
            values_to = "shared_sites"
        ) |>
        filter(cell_1 != cell_2) |>
        separate(dataset, into = c("sample", "cutoff"), sep = "_") %>%
        mutate(cutoff = factor(cutoff, levels = c("1", "2", "5", "10", "20")))

    return(dataset)
}

shared_sites <-
    lapply(
        shared_files,
        parse_shared
    ) %>%
    bind_rows()

for (this_sample in unique(shared_sites$sample)) {
    shared_sites %>%
        filter(sample == this_sample & cutoff == 1) %>%
        mutate(shared_sites = as.integer(shared_sites)) %>%
        select(cell_1, cell_2, shared_sites) %>%
        pivot_wider(
            names_from = cell_2,
            values_from = shared_sites,
            values_fill = NA
        ) %>%
        column_to_rownames("cell_1") %>%
        pheatmap::pheatmap(
            silent = TRUE,
            display_numbers = TRUE,
            fontsize_number = 2,
            number_format =  "%.0f",
            fontsize = 5,
            filename = paste0(
                "output/figures/shared_sites/shared_sites_",
                this_sample,
                "_c1.pdf"
            ),
            width = 10,
            height = 10,
            main = paste0(
                "Number of Sites Shared Between Individual Cells for Sample ",
                this_sample
            )
        )
}

shared_sites_histograms <-

    ggplot(

        )

        ~ cutoff,

        scales = "free_y"
    ) +
    labs(
        title = "Distribution of Number of Genomic Positions With Shared Variant\nInformation Between Two Cells",
        subtitle = "For sites where either cell has a non-reference variant call",
        x = "Shared covered genomic positions",
        y = "Count",
        fill = "Minimum read depth\nto call variants"
    ) +
    theme(
        legend.position = "none"
    )

ggsave(

)

:::

I want to look over the merged bcfs and quantify the proportion of positions covered by n reads has a variant call.

Then I want to compare these values between the flex data, where any variant call is artifactual and the B6 data, where an unknown proportion of variant calls at any depth are artifactual. This will allow me to estimate the false positive rate for SNV calls in the pipeline.

Downsample each sample to a range of cells per cluster

This is to test the minimum number of cells/reads needed to accurately identify genetically distinct populations.

Also, I will use the data where I downsample to one cell to calculate coverage provided by one cell on average

Here I am going to downsample the mouse samples to varying number of cells per cluster to run scanBit

This is to test how low we can go while the algorithm still works and provide bcf files to use to quantify coverage per cell in later analyses ::: {.cell}

Code
merged_sobj_mouse_ctrls <-
    qs::qread("output/seurat_objects/merged/merged_norm_mouse.qs")

min_n_cells <- 500

keep_clusters <-
    merged_sobj_mouse_ctrls$cell_group %>%
    table() %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    filter(Freq > min_n_cells) %>%
    pull(".")

# Keep only clusters with > min_n_cells cells
merged_sobj_mouse_ctrls <-
    merged_sobj_mouse_ctrls %>%
    subset(cell_group %in% keep_clusters)

# Here, 500000 is forcing us to keep all the cells, so functions as a control
n_cell_cutoffs <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 500, 500000)

output <- scanbit_downsample_loop(
    merged_sobj_mouse_ctrls,
    cutoff_vector = n_cell_cutoffs,
    out_dir_base = "output/downsample/scanbit_out/mouse/",
    sample_label = "mouse",
    min_read_depth = 10,
    ploidy = "mm10",
    ref_fasta = "/home/gdrobertslab/lab/GenRef/10x-mm10/fasta/genome.fa"
)

samples_geo <-

    pull(Sample_ID) %>%

min_n_cells <- 200

n_cell_cutoffs <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 500, 500000)

output <-
    parallel::mclapply(
        samples_geo,
        mc.cores = 5,
        mc.preschedule = FALSE,
        function(this_sample) {
            sobj <-
                qs::qread(paste0(
                    "output/seurat_objects/individual/",
                    this_sample,
                    "_human.qs"
                ))

            sobj$cell_group <- paste0("clust_", sobj$individ_clusters)

            keep_clusters <-
                sobj$cell_group %>%
                table() %>%
                as.data.frame() %>%
                filter(Freq > min_n_cells) %>%
                pull(".")

            # Keep only clusters with > min_n_cells cells
            sobj <-
                sobj %>%
                subset(cell_group %in% keep_clusters)

            Idents(sobj) <-
                sobj$cell_group

            scanbit_downsample_loop(
                sobj,
                cutoff_vector = n_cell_cutoffs,
                out_dir_base = file.path(
                    "output/downsample/scanbit_out/geo_samples/",
                    this_sample
                ),
                sample_label = this_sample,
                ploidy = "GRCh38",
                min_read_depth = 10,
                ref_fasta = "/home/gdrobertslab/lab/GenRef/10x-hg38/fasta/genome.fa"
            )
        }
    )

Show how bootstrap values degrade with decreasing cell count and UMI per pseudobulked cluster

The data were gathered by hand since I don’t have a programatic way to pull the top node bootstrap values out of the pdfs ::: {.cell}

rna_per_run <-
    list.files(
        path = "output/downsample/scanbit_out",
        pattern = "cell_barcode_table*",
        recursive = TRUE,
        full.names = TRUE
    ) %>%
    read_tsv(id = "run") %>%
    select(-cell_barcode, -bam_file) %>%
    mutate(
        run = basename(run) %>%
            str_remove("cell_barcode_table_") %>%
            str_remove("_cells.txt")
    ) %>%
    separate_wider_delim(
        run,
        delim = "_",
        names = c("sample", "cells")
    ) %>%
    mutate(cells = as.numeric(cells)) %>%
    group_by(sample, cells, cell_group) %>%
    summarize(total_umi = sum(nCount_RNA), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(sample, cells) %>%
    summarize(mean_umi = mean(total_umi), .groups = "drop")

transgene_panel_plot <- function(sobj, sample_name, plot_point_size = 0.5) {
    panel_plot <-
        ((
            DimPlot(
                sobj,
                group.by = "cell_group",
                pt.size = plot_point_size,
                label = TRUE,
                label.box = TRUE,
                repel = TRUE
            ) +
                NoLegend() +
                coord_fixed()
        ) +
            (
                DimPlot(
                    sobj,
                    group.by = "tumor_cell",
                    pt.size = plot_point_size,
                    label = TRUE,
                    label.box = TRUE,
                    repel = TRUE
                ) +
                    NoLegend() +
                    coord_fixed()
            )) /
            ((
                DimPlot(
                    sobj,
                    group.by = "snv_top_lvl_group_10",
                    pt.size = plot_point_size,
                    label = TRUE,
                    label.box = TRUE,
                    repel = TRUE
                ) +
                    NoLegend() +
                    coord_fixed()
            ) +
                (
                    FeaturePlot(
                        sobj,
                        features = "tumor_marker_count",
                        order = TRUE,
                        pt.size = plot_point_size
                    ) +
                        coord_fixed()
                ))

    ggplot2::ggsave(
        paste0("output/figures/transgene/", sample_name, "_plots.pdf"),
        plot = panel_plot,
        width = 15,
        height = 15
    )

    return()
}

sobj_list <- list()
for (this_sample in transgene_samples) {
    sobj_list[[this_sample]] <-
        qs::qread(paste0(
            "output/seurat_objects/individual/",
            this_sample,
            "_mouse.qs"
        )) %>%
        PercentageFeatureSet(pattern = "^tumor", col.name = "tumor_marker_pct")

    sobj_list[[this_sample]]$cell_group <- paste0(
        sobj_list[[this_sample]]$cluster_label,
        "_c",
        sobj_list[[this_sample]]$individ_clusters
    )

    for (this_cutoff in c(5, 10, 20, 30)) {
        sobj_list[[this_sample]] <- add_snv_group_to_sobj(
            sobj_list[[this_sample]],
            snv_group_file = paste0(
                "output/snv/transgene/snvs_",
                this_sample,
                "_",
                this_cutoff,
                "_groups.txt"
            ),
            new_columns = paste0(
                c("snv_group_", "snv_top_lvl_group_"),
                this_cutoff
            ),
            cell_group = "cell_group"
        )
    }

    tumor_markers <-
        grep(
            "^tumor",
            rownames(sobj_list[[this_sample]]),
            value = TRUE
        )

    if (length(tumor_markers) > 0) {
        sobj_list[[this_sample]]$tumor_marker_count <-
            FetchData(
                sobj_list[[this_sample]],
                vars = tumor_markers,
                layer = "counts"
            ) %>%
            rowSums()

        sobj_list[[this_sample]]$tumor_cell <-
            if_else(
                sobj_list[[this_sample]]$tumor_marker_count > 0,
                "Has transgene",
                "No transgene"
            )

        transgene_panel_plot(
            sobj_list[[this_sample]],
            this_sample,
            plot_point_size
        )
    } else {
        sobj_list[[this_sample]] <- NULL
    }
}

Code
ltbc_samples <- c("S0260", "S0261")

plot_point_size <- 0.5

marker_table <-
    parallel::mclapply(
        ltbc_samples,
        mc.cores = 2,
        function(this_sample) {
            sobj <-
                qs::qread(paste0(
                    "output/seurat_objects/individual/",
                    this_sample,
                    "_mouse.qs"
                ))

            ltbc_table <- gen_cellecta_bc_data(
                paste0(
                    "/home/gdrobertslab/lab/Counts_2/",
                    this_sample,
                    "/possorted_genome_bam.bam"
                ),
                samtools_module = "GCC/9.3.0 SAMtools/1.10", verbose = TRUE
            )

            ltbc_sub <-
                ltbc_table %>%
                mutate(
                    cid = paste0(cid, "-1"),
                    barcode = paste0(lt_14, "_", lt_30),
                    has_barcode = TRUE
                ) %>%
                select(-lt_14, -lt_30) %>%
                group_by(cid) %>%
                mutate(tumor_marker_count = n()) %>%
                slice_head(n = 1) %>%
                column_to_rownames("cid")

            sobj <-
                AddMetaData(
                    sobj,
                    ltbc_sub
                )

            # replace data missing from ltbc_table with values
            sobj$tumor_marker_count <-
                if_else(
                    is.na(sobj$tumor_marker_count),
                    0,
                    sobj$tumor_marker_count
                )

            sobj$has_barcode <-
                if_else(
                    is.na(sobj$has_barcode),
                    FALSE,
                    sobj$has_barcode
                )

            sobj$tumor_cell <-
                if_else(
                    sobj$has_barcode == TRUE,
                    "Has transgene",
                    "No transgene"
                )

            sobj$cell_group <- paste0(
                sobj$cluster_label,
                "_c",
                sobj$individ_clusters
            )

            for (this_cutoff in c(5, 10, 20, 30)) {
                sobj <- add_snv_group_to_sobj(
                    sobj,
                    snv_group_file = paste0(
                        "output/snv/transgene/snvs_",
                        this_sample,
                        "_",
                        this_cutoff,
                        "_groups.txt"
                    ),
                    new_columns = paste0(
                        c("snv_group_", "snv_top_lvl_group_"),
                        this_cutoff
                    ),
                    cell_group = "cell_group"
                )
            }

            transgene_panel_plot(
                sobj,
                this_sample,
                plot_point_size
            )

            marker_table <-
                sobj@meta.data %>%
                as_tibble() %>%
                select(
                    Sample_ID,
                    tumor_cell,
                    individ_clusters,
                    cluster_label
                ) %>%
                mutate(
                    cell_group =
                        paste0(
                            cluster_label,
                            "_c",
                            individ_clusters
                        )
                ) %>%
                select(-individ_clusters, cluster_label) %>%
                group_by(Sample_ID, cell_group, tumor_cell) %>%
                summarize(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
                group_by(Sample_ID, cell_group) %>%
                mutate(proportion = n / sum(n)) %>%
                filter(tumor_cell == "Has transgene") %>%
                arrange(desc(proportion))

            return(marker_table)
        }
    ) %>%
    bind_rows()

write_tsv(
    marker_table,
    "output/snv_processing/transgene/transgene_tumor_clust_ltbc.txt"
)

    height = 6
)

dodge_width <- 0.75

bootstrap_boxplot <-
    read_tsv(
        "output/human_bootstraps.txt",
        show_col_types = FALSE
    ) %>%
    #filter(!sample %in% c("G0039", "G0040", "G0041", "G0042", "G0043")) %>% # low quality samples
    pivot_longer(
        cols = -sample,
        names_to = "cutoff",
        values_to = "bootstrap"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
        cutoff = str_remove(cutoff, "c") %>%
            factor(levels = c("5", "10", "20", "30"))
    ) %>%
    left_join(
        read_tsv(
            "misc/validation_geo_metadata.tsv",
            show_col_types = FALSE
        ) %>%
            select("Sample_ID", "tumor_type", "sample_group") %>%
            distinct() %>%
            filter(
                sample_group %in%
                    c("tumor validation", "healthy samples")
            ) %>%
            rename(sample = "Sample_ID") %>%
            mutate(
                sample_group = str_remove(sample_group, " .+") %>%
                    str_to_sentence(),
                tumor_type = str_replace(tumor_type, "healthy", "Healthy") %>%
                    as.factor() %>%
                    fct_relevel("Healthy"),
            ),
        by = "sample"
    ) %>%
    ggplot(
        aes(
            x = cutoff,
            y = bootstrap,
            fill = tumor_type
        )
    ) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 85, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
    geom_boxplot(
        position = position_dodge(width = dodge_width),
        outlier.alpha = 0,
        alpha = 0.5
    ) +
    geom_point(
        aes(
            group = tumor_type,
            color = tumor_type
        ),
        position = ggbeeswarm::position_beeswarm(
            dodge.width = dodge_width,
            cex = 0.1
        ),
        alpha = 1
    ) +
    labs(
        x = "Minimum read depth cutoff",
        y = "Top node bootstrap value",
        title = "Top Node Bootstrap Value of Human Tumor and Normal Samples",
        color = "Tumor type"
    )

ggsave(
    "output/figures/human_bootstrap_boxplot2.pdf",
    bootstrap_boxplot,
    width = 8,
    height = 4
)

        sep = ","
    ),
    other_job_header_options = c("--time=05:00:00"),

g41 <- qs::qread("output/seurat_objects/individual/G0041_human.qs")
g41_cell_barcodes <-
    g41 %>%
    colnames() %>%
    paste(collapse = " ")

# I should filter variable_variants_file before I give it to call_variants_single_cell

call_variants_single_cell(
    bam_to_use = "output/cellranger_out/G0041/possorted_genome_bam.bam",
    variable_variants_file = "output/snv/human/mergedsnvs_G0041_variable_variants.tsv",
    cell_barcodes = g41_cell_barcodes,
    output_file = "cell_variant_calls_g41.tsv",
    min_depth = 3,
    variant_diff_cutoff = 1,
    ploidy = "GRCh38",
    ref_fasta = "/home/gdrobertslab/lab/GenRef/10x-hg38/fasta/genome.fa",
    job_base = "cell_vars",
    log_base = "slurm_cell_vars",
    # temp_dir = "output/temp/cell_vars_59",
    submit = TRUE,
    other_job_header_options = c("--time=12:00:00"),
    other_batch_options = c( # Just here as examples of things you might put
        "module purge",
        "module load miniforge3",
        'eval "$(conda shell.bash hook)"'
    )
)

count_to_call <-
    c(
        "0" = "0/0",
        "1" = "0/1",
        "2" = "1/1"
    )

genotype_info <-
    read_tsv(
        "output/snv/human/mergedsnvs_G0041_variable_variants.tsv",
        show_col_types = FALSE
    ) %>%
    filter(cross_minus_within_dist >= 1) %>%
    select(
        -group_1_within_dist,
        -group_2_within_dist,
        -cross_group_dist,
        -within_groups_mean_dist,
        -cross_minus_within_dist
    ) %>%
    mutate(
        mean_group_1_alts = round(mean_group_1_alts),
        mean_group_2_alts = round(mean_group_2_alts),
        group_1_genotype = count_to_call[as.character(mean_group_1_alts)],
        group_2_genotype = count_to_call[as.character(mean_group_2_alts)],
        pos = paste(chr, pos, sep = "_")
    )

tumor_genotype_profile <-
    genotype_info %>%
    pull(group_1_genotype, name = pos)

normal_genotype_profile <-
    genotype_info %>%
    pull(group_2_genotype, name = pos)

single_call_meta <-
    read_tsv(
        "cell_variant_calls_g41.tsv",
        show_col_types = FALSE
    ) %>%
    mutate(
        pos = paste(chr, pos, sep = "_"),
        tumor_genotype = tumor_genotype_profile[pos],
        normal_genotype = normal_genotype_profile[pos],
        call = if_else(
            call == 1,
            "0/1",
            call
        )
    ) %>%
    mutate(
        call = if_else(
            call == 0,
            "0/0",
            call
        )
    ) %>%
    select(-chr, -ref, -alt) %>%
    select(-tumor_genotype, -normal_genotype) %>%
    pivot_wider( # !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!This is making a tibble with a bunch of lists for columns
        id_cols = c(cell_barcode),
        names_from = pos,
        values_from = call
    ) %>%
    column_to_rownames("cell_barcode")

single_call_meta <- single_call_meta[colnames(g41), ]


g41$test <- single_call_meta$chrM_13071
g412 <- AddMetaData(g41, single_call_meta[, 1:10])
g41$has_calls <- !is.na(g41$prop_tumor_call)
g41$prop_tumor_call[!g41$has_calls] <- 0.1

sample_names <-

        show_col_types = FALSE
    ) %>%
    pull(sample)

cluster_ncounts <-
    parallel::mclapply(
        sample_names,
        mc.preschedule = FALSE,
        mc.cores = 5,
        function(x) {
            qs::qread(paste0(
                "output/seurat_objects/individual/",
                x,
                "_human.qs"
            ))@meta.data %>%
                group_by(Sample_ID, individ_clusters) %>%
                summarize(
                    mean_ncount = mean(nCount_RNA),
                    median_ncount = median(nCount_RNA),
                    sum_ncount = sum(nCount_RNA),
                    .groups = "drop"
                )
        }
    ) %>%
    bind_rows()

Quantify average run time and RAM usage

Delete failed runs so they don’t throw off our average

Code
del_files=($(grep FAILED \
    /gpfs0/scratch/mvc002/scanbit/*/slurmOut/*_mpileup-*.out \
    output/snv/mouse/tempdir/slurmOut/*_mpileup-*.out \
    | perl -pe 's/:.+//' \
    | uniq))

if [ ${#del_files[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    rm -- "${del_files[@]}"
fi
Code
grep \
    "Elapsed seconds" \
    /gpfs0/scratch/mvc002/scanbit/*/slurmOut/*_mpileup-*.out \
    output/snv/mouse/tempdir/slurmOut/*_mpileup-*.out \
    | perl -pe 's/:Elapsed seconds://' \
    | cut -f 2 -d " " \
    | numberStats.pl \
    > output/counts/mpileup_time.txt

I’m grepping M; here because slurm output double summaries for a couple samples ::: {.cell}

Code
grep \
    "Maximum CPU Memory" \
    /gpfs0/scratch/mvc002/scanbit/*/slurmOut/*_mpileup-*.out \
    output/snv/mouse/tempdir/slurmOut/*_mpileup-*.out \
    | grep "M;" \
    | perl -pe 's/.+Maximum CPU Memory://' \
    | perl -pe 's/M;.+//' \
    | numberStats.pl \
    > output/counts/mpileup_ram_M.txt
